title: Draw a caret in the menu header, and let the query be edited
head: f98402b8f418
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Short query prefix makes the long suffix unnecessarily disappear during elision
leads.consequence: With textRoom=200 px, a 10 px prefix and a suffix whose implicit width is at least 200 px, headRoom=100, queryHead occupies only 10, and queryTail gets 100. Row lays out 110 px of text inside a 200 px allowance, leaving 90 unused px while eliding the tail. Moving one step from an empty head can suddenly halve the visible suffix. Cap the reserved head allocation by headWant, then let the suffix take the remainder.

leads.summary: Coordinate the masked secret-input PR before accepting either header implementation
leads.consequence: Open #12698 adds mode=secret and promises masking by substituting bullet characters in the old header Text. Its merge with this head has a conflict precisely on that Text versus this Row. Choosing this Row while retaining #12698's secret mode paints both unmasked filterText slices before Tab reveals anything, defeating the secret-input guarantee; choosing the old Text drops this PR's caret. A combined header must apply the mask to both halves, with the reveal flag, and test both modes. This is an integration warning, not a leak in the pinned head alone.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus Q4; published in related PRs

leads.summary: Restored search from #12759 needs a saved caret, and its Left branch preempts movement
leads.consequence: #12759 deliberately makes Left navigate even while a query is active, which disagrees with the caret PR's Left movement. In a three-way merged copy with only the setActiveMenu signature conflict resolved, #12759's `Left && !dmenuActive` branch runs before moveCaret, so Left navigates instead of editing the query; this PR's menu-caret test fails. Separately, its restoredFilter writes directly to filterText after entering a submenu cleared it and clamped caretPos to 0, so going back to a nonempty saved search inserts the next character at its beginning. The PRs need an explicit navigation choice and must save/restore caretPos with the query.
leads.triage: new; verified by coordinator from #12759 diff (direct assignment, Left branch) and head Menu.qml:73 clamp; Opus self-check confirmed via merge-tree that the Left branches auto-merge with #12759 first; published with qualifier

leads.summary: The IME TextInput PR changes the same input and header ownership
leads.consequence: Open #12338 transfers focus to TextInput, forwards keys and delegates printable text, paste and IME commits to TextInput. This PR retains a focused Item, manually consumes one-unit event.text and renders a Row. Three conflicts appear in a three-way merge: insertion helpers versus resetFilter, printable-key interception versus TextInput editing, and Row versus TextInput. Keeping this PR's key handler/header drops #12338's IME and paste input; keeping TextInput's forced end position loses caret editing. Neither is a harmless same-line rebase. Design a single input owner before combining.

leads.summary: Overlapping printable-key PRs require preserving both modifier fixes and insertion at caret
leads.consequence: Both open PRs modify the exact printable-event branch this PR changes. The three-way merge with #8023 conflicts there: choosing its side calls setFilter(filterText + event.text) and silently restores append-only typing when the caret is in the middle; choosing this PR's side loses #8023's KeypadModifier/GroupSwitchModifier acceptance and fails its new menu-input assertion. #7659 changes the same predicate for the same keypad/AltGr class. The combined condition should use the widened modifier acceptance while calling insertAtCaret.
leads.triage: merged with Opus rebase-conflict list; published as ordinary rebase conflicts

leads.summary: The new test passes even if the QML insertion handler ignores every typed character
leads.consequence: Helper unit tests call caretInsert directly and screen-wiring tests inspect unrelated regular expressions, but none assert that insertAtCaret actually passes the helper's result to setFilter. In an owned mutant, replacing its body with `root.setFilter(root.filterText)` drops every printable character yet the new caret test, kept menu test and QML text-format scan all exit 0. Add a test of the actual handler/data flow (or a QML event fixture) that fails for this mutant.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F3; published as Optional test improvement

leads.summary: Document the new caret test in the menu's explicit test list
leads.consequence: The menu development guide says only menu-test.sh and menu-guards-test.sh exercise MenuModel directly, but this PR adds menu-caret-test.sh with direct calls to the new exported functions. Add `menu-caret-test.sh` to the list at line 13; this is documentation/fixture coverage, not a test-run registration problem (test/shell discovers it automatically).
leads.triage: verified (docs/menu.md:10-13 names two test files in prose); dropped as nitpick

leads.summary: Calculator PR has an export-list conflict when combined with caret helpers
leads.consequence: #10294's QML calculator calls calcResultForQuery and its Node fixture calls the exported method. Merging the JS code bodies succeeds, but the module.exports list conflicts: choosing just the caret side makes its fixture throw `menu.calcResultForQuery is not a function`; choosing just calculator exports makes this PR's caret test fail. Both sets of exports are required. This is a trivial but real integration conflict, not a current-head calculator defect.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** The caret works as described in the tested scope. Typing, Backspace and Ctrl+Backspace act at the caret, Ctrl+U still clears the query, and Left/Right, Ctrl+Left/Right, Home and End move it. The caret blinks, goes solid on each edit or move, and is hidden while the delete confirmation is open. The `MenuModel.js` helpers stay within `[0, length]` for stale, negative and past-the-end indices. With the caret at the end of the query, which is the only state the base could be in, every other key behaves as before, including Right, Enter, Escape, Delete and the dmenu modes. The PR merges cleanly onto current `quattro` (`3faafba2`), and the menu tests pass there.

Two behaviour issues and one test gap are below.

### Text after the caret is cut off at half width in a long query

When the query is wider than the header and the text before the caret is narrower than half the header, the text after the caret is capped at half the available width, even though the text before the caret uses much less. The rest of the header stays blank.

Once the query overflows, `headRoom` reserves at least `textRoom / 2` for the text before the caret, unless the caret is at the start. `queryTail` then gets `textRoom - headRoom`, regardless of how wide `queryHead` actually renders:

```qml
readonly property real headRoom: headWant + tailWant <= textRoom
  ? headWant
  : Math.max(textRoom - tailWant, textRoom / 2)
...
width: Math.min(implicitWidth, Math.max(0, headerRow.textRoom - headerRow.headRoom))   // queryTail
```

The PR's header `Row` was rendered offscreen in Qt 6.11.2, with a 16 px heading, a 264 px header and a 56-character query in a monospace font:

| Caret position | Text after the caret | Unused header width |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `c│onvert 100 u…` | about 121 px (nearly half) |
| 8 | cut off at the same half-width cap | about 54 px |
| 0, middle, end | fills the header | 0 px |

**Impact:** Cosmetic, but it shows up when going back to fix something near the start of a long query, which is the case the PR is built for.

**Suggested change:** Give the tail the room the head actually uses:

```qml
width: Math.min(implicitWidth, Math.max(0, headerRow.textRoom - queryHead.width))
```

In the same harness this fills the header at caret positions 1 and 8, and it does not change the other rendered cases. Moving the width split into `MenuModel.js` as a pure function would also let the node tests cover it.

### Holding Right runs past the end of the query and activates the row

Right now moves the caret, so holding it is a natural way to reach the end of the query. The handler does not check `event.isAutoRepeat`. Once the caret reaches the end, the next auto-repeated Right takes the existing activation branch. Qt's Wayland client delivers held keys as repeat events.

```text
Holding Right, menu query "fire|fox":
  press   -> caret 4
  repeat  -> caret 5
  repeat  -> caret 6
  repeat  -> caret 7 (end)
  repeat  -> activateIndex(0): the top result runs or its submenu opens

dmenu input mode, "ab| cd":
  caret 3, 4, 5 (end), then applyDmenuSelection("ab cd"): the prompt is submitted
```

This sequence comes from running the PR's key handler code in node with stubs. It was not observed on a live desktop.

**Impact:** Holding Right to reach the end can launch the top search result, or submit a dmenu input prompt, without a separate key press.

**Suggested change:** Keep activation for a fresh press only. For example, send `event.key === Qt.Key_Right && (root.caretPos < root.filterText.length || event.isAutoRepeat)` to `moveCaret`, which does nothing at the end. A new Right press at the end still activates as before.

**Optional test improvement:** The new assertions cover the `MenuModel.js` arithmetic, but not the typing, Backspace, Left caret move or Home/End wiring. With the typing branch reverted to `root.setFilter(root.filterText + event.text)`, `menu-caret-test.sh` and `menu-test.sh` still pass. The same holds for Backspace reverted to deleting at the end, the Home/End branches removed, or the Left caret move removed. Asserting on the `root.insertAtCaret(event.text)`, `root.editFilterAtCaret(event)`, Left `moveCaret(event, -1)` and Home/End call sites would catch those regressions.

**Description note:** The description lists Home/End among the tested cases, but no assertion covers Home or End. The two "stops at the start/end" assertions test `caretStep` bounds. Left's go-back reflex is also unchanged rather than narrowed: on the base, Left already went back only when the query was empty.

### Related open PRs

- **#12338** makes the header a `TextInput` so input methods work, and deliberately shows no caret. It conflicts with this PR in three `Menu.qml` hunks. Because a `TextInput` already provides a cursor, cursor movement and IME support, the two PRs are alternative designs for the same header.
- **#12759** makes Left go back in regular menus even while a search is active, the opposite of this PR's Left caret move. Git merges the two Left branches without a textual conflict, and #12759's branch comes first, so the caret move would silently stop working in regular menus. #12759 also restores the parent menu's query with a direct `root.filterText = ...` assignment. This PR's `onFilterTextChanged` clamp only moves the caret down, so after a restore the caret keeps its old position (0 when the submenu query was empty) instead of moving to the end, and the next character can land at the start. If both land, the Left semantics need a deliberate choice and the restore path also needs to set `caretPos`.
- **#12698** (masked input mode) rewrites the same header `text:` binding to draw bullets. If both land, the masking has to cover both `queryHead` and `queryTail`, or the masked text shows in plain form.
- **#7659**, **#8023** and **#12574** change the typed-character condition on the line this PR edits. **#10294** conflicts in the `MenuModel.js` exports list. These are ordinary rebase conflicts.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of head `f98402b8` against base `6ea32155` and current `quattro` (`3faafba2`). The menu tests were run at head and on head merged onto current `quattro`, with targeted mutations of the key wiring. The PR's header `Row` was rendered in an offscreen Qt 6.11.2 harness with the default style sizes. The key handler was run in node with stubs for 21 keys in six menu states. No live desktop session, real key auto-repeat or input-method test.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
